title: Custom XDR union switched on a float, with discriminant 0.1, must be refused
caps_note: An XDR language rule (RFC 4506 section 4.15: a union discriminant is int, unsigned int, enum or bool), not a CAP; Stellar's own unions never switch on a float.
why: RFC 4506 allows only integer, enum and bool union discriminants; an XDR runtime that lets a schema switch on a float encodes a discriminant that does not round-trip (0.1 decodes as 0.10000000149011612).

known_divergences.detail: Executed against the js-xdr each SDK version installs (4.0.0 for 16.x, 5.0.0 for 17.x): a union with switchOn float() and a case 0.1 is accepted, encodes the discriminant as 3dcccccd, and decoding those bytes fails ('no case for union discriminator 0.10000000149011612'). Fixed in js-xdr by pull request #171 (906a0aae), not released; no conformance driver offers this op yet, so the runner lists it as not exercised.
known_divergences.evidence: hand run of js-xdr union('U', {switchOn: float(), cases: [unionCase('a', 0.1, void())]}) with encode({type: 0.1}) then decode, in each JavaScript column's installed js-xdr

notes: Built by xdrcheck-corpus synth from corpus/recipes/xdr-strict/api-float-union-discriminant-custom-schema.json. Origin: js-xdr#162. Arguments of xdr.custom_union_encode, defined by this entry: switch_on is the XDR type the union switches on (here float); cases lists the union's arms as {discriminant (tagged number), arm (an XDR type name, here void)}; discriminant is the value to encode, then decode. Conforming: the runtime refuses the schema or the value. This is "union discriminants that accept floats" taken literally; it cannot occur with Stellar's own types or in wire bytes. Expected values were computed from the XDR definitions, the CAP or SEP text and the stellar-core rule cited under related, with an independent encoder; no SDK output was used.
